Data provenance & scientific limitations
Loading…

The comparison is a curated archival pair, not a current all-sky SPHEREx feed. Images are reprojected to the same sky grid with a shared display stretch. Detector wavelength varies across the field; brightness differences are not evidence of variability. Registration errors, noise, masks and instrumental effects can create apparent changes. No automatic planet discovery is claimed.

THE BIG PICTURE

102 colours.
An entire sky.

SPHEREx surveys the sky in 102 near-infrared spectral channels, investigating cosmic history, galaxies and the ingredients for life.

The NASA Space Apps Challenge brings people together to solve problems using open space and Earth-science data. “Planet X and SPHEREx” asks for a public tool that makes changes across sky images easy to explore.

This independent prototype uses real SPHEREx data for the featured comparison and 2MASS/DSS2 for full-sky navigation. It is not a NASA product.
